transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. It's nice to meet you. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. I, um... well, I'm here because of work. I drive a forklift down at the warehouse, have for years, and... I just want to make sure I'm explaining this right, so please let me know if I'm not making sense. But lately, the routing system we use, it... it feels like it's not just a computer anymore. I know it sounds a little strange, but I really believe it's been marking my moves. Like it's sending messages through the scanners to push me out, just because I'm one of the older guys there. Is that... does that sound like something you can help me with? I just want to be a good worker again.
How long have you been noticing these feelings that the routing system is sending you messages?

Well, Doctor, I... I hope it doesn't make me sound too far gone. I really don't want you to think poorly of me, I'm usually a very level-headed guy. But it's been a little while now. I'd say it's been about a year and eight months since I first started having these... these fixed beliefs about the scanners. 

And, um... I should probably tell you this, just so I'm giving you all the right information and doing what I'm supposed to do. It's not just the messages. Sometimes there are... well, voices, too. They've been with me for that same amount of time, a year and eight months. I know saying that probably sounds terrible, doesn't it? I really try my best to just keep my head down and ignore them so I can do a good job, I promise. Am I... am I giving you the kind of answers you need?
During this past year and eight months, have you been using any alcohol, drugs, or other substances regularly?

Oh, no, Doctor, not at all. I know how bad that stuff can be, and I really wouldn't want to mess up my job or my health like that. I've always tried to be a responsible guy, you know? I might have a beer with dinner once in a blue moon, but that's it, I swear. No drugs or anything like that. I really hope you believe me. I just want to make sure I'm doing everything right to get back to normal. Is that... is that okay? Did I answer that right?
During this past year and eight months, have you had any periods of feeling very depressed, hopeless, or unusually elated/energetic that lasted for a couple of weeks or more?

Well, I... I definitely haven't been unusually energetic or anything like that. I've always been a steady worker, not the type to get all worked up or act out of sorts. But, um... I guess I have been feeling a bit down. 

I really hate to complain, because I know there are people out there with real problems, and I don't want to sound like I'm just whining. But since you asked... it's been a while. About two years and a month, actually. It started not long after they changed up the schedules at the warehouse and it just started wearing me down. It's just been hanging over me since then. I try to put on a brave face and just push through it at work, I really do. I hope that doesn't make me sound weak or anything. Is it normal to feel like that when things get tough at work? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
Have there been times in the past year and eight months when you were having the voices or the belief about the scanners, but you were NOT feeling depressed or down at all?

Well, um... yes, I suppose there was. I really hope it doesn't make me sound too crazy, Doctor. I want to be completely honest with you so you can help me, but it's hard to talk about. 

There was a stretch a while back where I actually felt like I was doing a bit better. My mood had eased up some, and I was eating normally again, talking a little more with the guys on my shift... I really thought I was getting back on track, you know? But, well... even during those few weeks when I wasn't feeling so down, I was still hearing dispatch calling my number when no one was there. And I still... I still believed the routing system was tracking my movements. 

I know how that sounds, I really do. I kept it to myself because I didn't want anyone to think I couldn't handle the job. I really try to be a good employee. Does that make sense, Doctor? Am I explaining it okay?
How long did that stretch last when you were hearing the voices and still believed the routing system was tracking you, but your mood had lifted and you weren't feeling depressed at all?

Well, um... I think it was for several weeks. Maybe a month or so? I really hope I'm remembering that right for you, Doctor. 

Like I said, my mood had eased up some, and I was eating my meals and talking a little more with the guys... I was really trying my best to just be normal and fit in. But for those several weeks, even when I wasn't feeling so down, I still heard dispatch calling my number, and I still couldn't shake the feeling that the routing system was tracking me. 

I really tried to ignore it, I promise. I just put my head down and kept driving the forklift. I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline so you can figure out what's wrong with me.

Aside from that one-month stretch when your mood lifted, has the depression been present continuously the rest of the time since the voices and beliefs about the routing system started, or have there been other periods without depression as well?

Well, um... I really don't want to make it sound like I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself all the time. I know I need to pull my weight. But, honestly... aside from that one month, it's pretty much been there the whole time. 

Even when the... the fears about the warehouse and the tracking got a little quieter for a bit, I just couldn't shake the heavy feeling. I was still feeling so down and just... empty, I guess. I couldn't even get myself back into the things I usually love. I used to do a lot of fishing, and woodworking in the garage, and I'd always be at the table for family meals. But for most of this whole trouble, I just haven't had it in me to do any of that. 

I feel terrible admitting that, because I know I should be doing more with my family and keeping active. I really try, Doctor, I do. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too difficult or ungrateful for the good days I did have.
During the times you've been feeling down, have you also noticed changes in your sleep, trouble concentrating, feelings of guilt or worthlessness, or thoughts of death or suicide?

Well, um... I really don't want you to think I'm just complaining, Doctor. I know I have a lot to be thankful for. But, yes... when the heavy feeling is there, it's hard not to think about things. 

I don't mean to sound dramatic, but I just... I keep going over every mistake I ever made. At the warehouse, at home... just everywhere. I try to be a good provider, a good husband, but lately I just feel like... like I've let everyone down. Sometimes I even think my family would have been better off if I hadn't messed things up so badly. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds awful. I really don't want you to think I'm a bad person or that I don't appreciate my family. I just... my mind gets stuck on all the things I did wrong. Is that... is that normal for what I'm going through? I hope I'm answering your question okay.
